summary: Rigid token ceilings can be economically irrational when one additional verification step prevents expensive rework or an incident.

points.text: Tokenization differs by provider and model, so a raw-token allowance is not a stable cross-model measure of money or computational effort.
Hard caps can bias agents toward premature answers, skipped tests or hidden retries unless completion criteria remain primary.
For low-volume, high-value tasks, engineering a fine-grained budget service may cost more than simple alerts and human approval.
